title: Denominator torsion in the kernel of first-localization cohomology
statement: Let R,A,Aq,B,D be commutative rings in one universe, with R-algebra structures on A,Aq,B, an A-algebra structure on Aq compatible with R, and algebra structures from A tensor_R B and Aq tensor_R B to D. Assume the R- and B-module derived categories exist. Let Q be a complex of A-modules and L,K base-derived tensor cohomology models [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model] for Q and Aq tensor_A Q. Let uQ be an R-complex map whose degree-j component sends x to 1 tensor x. For i in Z let c be the B-linear cohomology map obtained by composing L.cohomologyIso(i), H^i of L.derived(uQ) followed by the unique universal-counit-compatible isomorphism L.derived -> K.derived, and K.cohomologyIso(i) inverse. Let S be a submonoid of A and Aq a localization of A at S. For x in L.cohomology(i) with c(x)=0 there exists s in S such that (s tensor 1)*x=0.

source.place: Tags 06Y6 and 0DJ8, derived change of rings and the affine cohomology localization identity

proof.text: Use the balanced-complex unit computation to obtain C and A-linear source/target cohomology isomorphisms. The commuting equation sends a class killed by localizationModelMap to a class killed by the ordinary complex scalar-extension unit.

Apply complexLocalizationUnit_kernel to that class. A-linearity and injectivity of the source isomorphism transport the denominator annihilation equation back to L.cohomology(i); the restricted A-action is includeLeft(s).
